interest: Shows 1941 marine war-risk rates as informal intelligence on Japanese expectations toward British naval seizure.
overview: Parker & Co. reports Japanese insurer Nippon Fire quoted 3% for war-risk coverage, including British seizure, on Calcutta-New York goatskin cargo via Kobe, below the 3.5% American rate excluding seizure, suggesting Japan expected no imminent clash with Britain.

people.name: J. Brooks B. Parker
people.role: Insurance underwriter and partner, Parker & Co.

subfiles.about: Personal covering note forwarding an enclosed commercial intelligence communication to the Department of State.
subfiles.summary: Parker forwards a marine-insurance rate report to Reed for referral to the appropriate State Department desk.
subfiles.title: Covering letter from Parker & Co. to Edward L. Reed enclosing communication for Department of State
subfiles.to: Edward L. Reed, Esq., Department of State

subfiles.about: Report informing the Secretary of State of low war risk insurance rates quoted by a Japanese insurer covering British seizure of cargo on Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Parker & Co. reports Nippon Fire Insurance quoted 3% war-risk coverage including British seizure for goatskin cargo from Calcutta via Kobe, below the 3.5% US rate, implying Japan saw no imminent British conflict.
subfiles.title: Letter from Parker & Co. to the Secretary of State regarding Japanese war risk marine insurance rates
